categories.categoryInsight: Layer 1s carry the largest community and ecosystem war chests in crypto: across these four, 46-66% of genesis supply sits in community, ecosystem, foundation, or treasury buckets (Aptos 51% community alone; Sui 66% across foundation-managed reserve, treasury, and community programs), because L1s must fund validators, grants, and developer ecosystems for a decade. Insider share (team plus investor rounds) clusters at 32-35% for the modern cohort (Aptos 32.5%, Sui 34%), with earlier or heavily VC-funded launches running higher (Solana ~48% including all private sale rounds, Celestia 53%). Vesting culture is the strictest of any category: a 1-year cliff for team and investors is standard, total vests run 3-4 years (Aptos foundation and community stretch to 10 years), and modern L1s (2022+) launched with exactly 0% of insider tokens liquid at TGE. TGE floats are low, roughly 13-20%, and genesis percentages dilute over time because every L1 here adds staking rewards or inflation on top of genesis supply.

categories.categoryInsight: L2 tokens launched with no public sale at all: every one of the four distributed via airdrop plus insider and treasury allocations, making the airdrop the de facto float mechanism (12.75% for ARB, 17.5% for ZK, 19% pledged for OP, 18% community provisions plus rebates for STRK). Combined team-plus-investor share is heavy and consistent, 33-45% (ZK 33.3%, OP 36%, STRK 38.2%, ARB 44.5%), and all four keep large DAO treasury or foundation pools (OP 45% ecosystem plus retroPGF, ARB 42.8% treasury plus foundation, ZK 49.2% Token Assembly plus Ecosystem). The vesting culture is a 1-year cliff then roughly 3 more years of monthly unlocks (ARB, ZK textbook cases); Starknet is the notorious outlier, with investor and early-contributor unlocks starting just two months after the February 2024 provisions launch. TGE floats are low (roughly 7-17%), so all four carry multi-year overhang, with full unlock schedules running into 2027-2029.

categories.categoryInsight: Top DeFi protocols consistently commit the majority of supply to community and ecosystem: Uniswap gave 60% to community members, dYdX 50%, and Hyperliquid roughly 76% including future emissions, with genesis airdrops of 15-31% fully unlocked on day one being a category signature. Insider share (team plus investors) clusters between 22% and 55%: Uniswap ~40%, dYdX ~50%, Ethena 55%, while Hyperliquid broke the pattern entirely with 23.8% to contributors and zero investor allocation. Vesting culture is standardized around 4-year schedules for insiders, usually with a ~1-year cliff (Ethena's 25% cliff at month 12, dYdX's lockup that first released 30% at month 27). TGE float varies dramatically by era: 2020-2021 launches floated little beyond the airdrop and produced violent cliff unlocks later (dYdX Dec 2023), while 2024 launches like Hyperliquid floated 31% at genesis to front-load distribution.

categories.categoryInsight: Gaming and metaverse tokens push an unusually large share of supply into gameplay and community emissions rather than insiders: AXS routes 49% to staking plus play-to-earn rewards, BEAM's genesis (Merit Circle) puts about 44% into community incentives, liquidity and retroactive rewards, and IMX dedicates 51.74% to ecosystem development. Insider share (team plus advisors) clusters at 20-29% and direct investor rounds are modest (4-21%), while public sales are small (4-12%) and typically ran through launchpad IEOs (Binance Launchpad for both AXS and SAND). Vesting culture is multi-year (4-5.5 year full unlock schedules) and this category has a notable habit of voluntarily extending insider lockups mid-cycle: Immutable re-locked a 125M IMX developer tranche in 2023 and Merit Circle re-cliffed core contributor tokens to 4 years. The category also contains projects with no fixed genesis allocation at all: Gala (GALA) was evaluated and excluded because it launched with no token sale or pre-mint, distributing purely via daily node emissions split 50/50 between node operators and the company, so it publishes no allocation chart.

categories.categoryInsight: AI & DePIN tokenomics splits into two eras: legacy networks (Render 2017) sold tokens with no vesting at all and kept most supply in network-controlled escrow, while modern launches (Worldcoin, io.net, Grass) follow the VC playbook with heavy locks. Combined insider share (team + investors) in the modern cohort runs 25-47% of supply: Worldcoin 25%, io.net ~34%, Grass 47%. Ultra-low floats are the category signature, from Worldcoin's ~1% TGE float to io.net's ~12% and Grass's ~24%, because 50-75% of supply is reserved for community/network incentives released via very long emission schedules (15 years for WLD community tokens, 20 years for IO supplier rewards). Team terms cluster around a 12-month cliff with 3-4 year total vesting; the notable outlier culture is fair launch, exemplified by Bittensor (TAO), which was excluded here precisely because 100% mined emission means no published allocation buckets exist.
